Subject: Request: Azure Private Marketplace seller onboarding + procurement path

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As discussed, Aelford is evaluating a private plan for our enterprise customers and we'd like to list Redwood's Private SKU in our Azure tenant. Can you share the seller authorization steps we need to complete on our side, plus the procurement path (PO, invoicing, and any marketplace entitlements) so procurement can start their intake?

Attached is a short intake from procurement with required fields. Key questions for us:
- Do we need a private offer procurement ID or is the standard private plan flow sufficient?
- What commercial terms require explicit signature (MSA vs marketplace contract)?
- Lead times for activation after PO vs after DocuSign signature?

Please loop in whoever owns marketplace contracts. We aim to have legal + procurement ready by next Tuesday (2026-08-18).

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Aelford Systems

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: Azure Private Marketplace seller onboarding + procurement path

Hi Alex — great to connect yesterday. Looping in Marcus (partner/onboarding) and Kimberly (commercial/legal) to help close the loop.

High-level answers:
- Seller authorization: Aelford will need to request a private offer from Redwood. We will submit a seller authorization request in the Azure portal on your behalf once we have the tenant ID and the authorized contact.
- Procurement path: We support DocuSign (preferred) for commercial terms + a marketplace-only acceptance path for standard entitlements. For enterprise private plans we typically require a short amendment + SOW (if there's design work) and an invoice/PO flow tied to the Marketplace billing account.
- Activation timing: In practice activation after DocuSign is faster (24-48h) because our ops team performs the entitlement mapping once countersigned. PO-only activation is possible but usually requires an acceptance workflow and can add 3-7 business days.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please share tenant ID and the procurement & licensing contact (Juliet?).
2) Alex: upload any redlines to the attached intake or send the redline doc directly.
3) Marcus: will prepare the seller checklist and expected timelines for entitlements.
4) Kimberly: can advise on any language we need to avoid in the marketplace listing (re: IP, indemnity, data processing).

I'll attach our seller checklist for Azure private plans for your procurement team.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Folks — reviewed Aelford's redline. Summary of suggested responses:
1) Net-60: acceptable for enterprise customers with a purchase order, but requires finance approval and a short credit intake (2–3 business days). We should confirm whether Aelford will sign a 1yr invoice commitment or prefers ad-hoc billing.
2) Data processing: Redwood needs a DPA for processing customer data; we can reference our standard DPA (link in checklist). For marketplace entitlements, we will not hold customer data on Aelford's tenant; processing is limited to telemetry and logs per the DPA.
3) Revenue recognition: Marketplace invoicing has Azure-specific revenue share timing. We can add a clause that finalizes manifests upon activation; however, Aelford's ask to shift revenue-recognition responsibilities to Redwood is non-standard — we should push back.

Action items:
- Marcus: prepare an activation timeline doc and confirm whether we need a short SOW for integration work.
- Lauren: confirm finance can accept net-60 pending credit intake.
- I'll draft a brief concession memo for Alex/Juliet to explain why we can't accept revenue-recognition shift and propose alternate language.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
